description: Provenance record for the historical USPTO patent bar (registration examination) sessions used as raw material for Phase 2 (historical exam extraction & current-law audit). These are the only registration-examination question sets USPTO is known to have ever officially released to the public. They predate the America Invents Act (2011) and the current MPEP edition, so questions here are NOT assumed to reflect current law -- see 'current_law_caveat' below. Do not treat this manifest's sources as exam-defining; the authoritative exam-defining sources remain those in reference/exam_source_manifest/manifest.json.
current_law_caveat: All three sessions below predate the America Invents Act (enacted 2011) and reflect the pre-AIA, first-to-invent patent system, older interference practice, and MPEP/37 CFR section numbering that has since changed or been repealed. Many questions and model answers are therefore obsolete under current law. Extraction (Phase 2, this pass) captures the raw question/answer/rationale text only, with no current-law judgment applied.

sessions.summary: 100/100 questions individually assessed against current law (MPEP 9th Ed. Rev. 01.2024, current USC/CFR, and post-2002 case law). 53 STILL_VALID, 26 PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE (doctrine intact, citation/terminology stale), 21 OBSOLETE (tested legal framework no longer applies, overwhelmingly due to the America Invents Act). Corrected 2026-09-04 during Phase 3 flashcard-promotion QA: 3 entries (AM-35, AM-43, PM-12) were found inconsistent with their own audit notes -- two had unfixed pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 paragraph citations and one (PM-12, nonsigning-inventor 37 CFR 1.47 practice) had a note that already said 'eliminated by the AIA' but a STILL_VALID status field; all three corrected (2 to PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE, 1 to OBSOLETE) -- see audit_note text in 2002-10-16_audit.json for detail.

100/100 questions individually assessed against current law (MPEP 9th Ed. Rev. 01.2024, current USC/CFR, and post-2003 case law), cross-checked against the local current-MPEP text corpus in mpep_build/ for specific rule/section claims. 49 STILL_VALID, 35 PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE (doctrine intact, citation/terminology stale -- notably pervasive pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 paragraph numbering, BPAI->PTAB renaming, and 37 CFR Part 10->Part 11 ethics-rule renumbering), 16 OBSOLETE (tested legal framework no longer applies -- pre-AIA priority-contest doctrine (102(g)/131 swearing-behind), pre-AIA 102(d)/(e) statutory-bar structure, pre-AIA 103(c) common-ownership exception, eliminated SIR and 37 CFR 1.47 practice, pre-AIA interference practice, the 2013 removal of the claim requirement for a nonprovisional filing date, and the 2015 design-patent-term change from 14 to 15 years). Corrected 2026-09-04 during Phase 3 QA: AM-30 and PM-29 moved from STILL_VALID to PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE (unfixed pre-AIA 112 paragraph citation; and an 'enabling disclosure' MPEP quote using the pre-AIA-only 'date of invention' formulation instead of the current dual AIA/pre-AIA formulation, respectively).

100/100 questions individually assessed against current law (MPEP 9th Ed. Rev. 01.2024, current USC/CFR, and post-2003 case law), cross-checked against the local current-MPEP text corpus in mpep_build/ for specific rule/section claims. 45 STILL_VALID, 35 PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE (doctrine intact, citation/terminology stale -- pre-AIA 102(e)/(g) and 103(c) renumbering, BPAI->PTAB renaming, appeal-rule relocation from 37 CFR 1.191-1.197 to Part 41, 112 paragraph renumbering to 112(a)/(b)/(d)/(f), the 2013 unification of 37 CFR 1.137's unavoidable/unintentional standards, the Dec. 2022 small-entity discount increase from 50% to 60%, and PAIR's Nov. 2022 retirement in favor of Patent Center), 20 OBSOLETE (tested legal framework no longer applies -- pre-AIA 102(d)/(g)/103(c) statutory frameworks, eliminated 37 CFR 1.47/1.99/1.131 practice, the pre-2004 PCT contracting-state designation requirement, the pre-2013 37 CFR 1.53(b) claim-for-filing-date requirement, the AIA's removal of citizenship from the inventor's oath, the AIA's removal of the 'in this country' geographic limitation on 102(a) prior art generally, and the pre-Bilski/Alice computer-related-invention eligibility framework of former MPEP 2106(IV)). Corrected 2026-09-04 during Phase 3 QA: 9 entries (AM-14, AM-18, AM-32, AM-35, PM-6, PM-25, PM-37, PM-38, PM-46) moved from STILL_VALID to PARTIALLY_OBSOLETE -- 7 had unfixed pre-AIA 112 paragraph citations, 1 (AM-18) quoted MPEP § 2121.01's enabling-disclosure test using only the pre-AIA 'date of invention' formulation, and 1 (PM-38) named the retired PAIR system in a distractor choice.

acquisition_method: USPTO originally hosted these PDFs at http://www.uspto.gov/ip/boards/oed/exam/past/ ; that path is no longer live on uspto.gov. All 12 files below were recovered from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) on 2026-09-03, using the CDX API (http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=uspto.gov/ip/boards/oed/exam/past/...) to find the archived snapshot timestamp for each file, then fetching the raw archived content via the 'id_' Wayback URL modifier (http://web.archive.org/web/<timestamp>id_/<original_url>), which serves the captured file without the Wayback toolbar/banner injection. Every fetched PDF was validated with pdfinfo (non-zero page count) and spot-checked with pdftotext against expected exam content before being committed.
cdx_search_note: The CDX index for this path shows question/answer PDFs archived ONLY for the three sessions below (October 2002, April 2003, October 2003). Result-statistics pages (pass/fail counts, not question content) exist in the CDX index for other administrations back to 1997, but no question or answer PDFs for those earlier sessions were ever archived at this path -- they appear not to have been placed online by USPTO in the first place, or were removed before any crawl captured them. Some third-party patent-bar prep sites claim to offer additional years (e.g. 1999-2001), but those are not traceable to an official USPTO release and were excluded from this acquisition per the project's source-provenance policy (see reference/exam_source_manifest/manifest.json).

extraction.script: reference/historical_exams/extract.py (parses am/pm questions + answers PDFs via pdftotext -layout into per-session JSON)
extraction.output: reference/historical_exams/extracted/<session_date>_<am|pm>.json -- one record per question: {session_date, part, number, stem, choices: {A-E}, answer, rationale, parse_warnings}
extraction.result: All 300 questions (6 files x 50 questions) parsed cleanly: 0 parse_warnings, 0 questions with a missing/empty stem, fewer than 4 choices, unparsed answer letter, or missing rationale, and 0 instances of page-header/footer text leaking into extracted fields (all verified programmatically, not just spot-checked).
